## About Me

My research sits at the intersection of signal processing, machine learning, and
clinical medicine. I work on diagnostic systems — particularly in computational
pathology for prostate cancer — that aim to be not only accurate, but interpretable,
verifiable, and deployable in the hospitals and laboratories that actually need them.
I am currently Principal Investigator of an HEC National Research Programme for
Universities (NRPU) project (2026–2028), building Pakistan's first expert-annotated
prostate cancer histopathology dataset and an AI-based diagnostic tool for Gleason
grading and perineural invasion detection, in partnership with King Edward Medical
University and Mayo Hospital, Lahore. See my full [Research Statement](research.qmd)
for more detail.

## Interests

- Computational pathology and whole-slide image analysis
- Deep learning for medical imaging, explainable AI
- Federated and privacy-preserving learning
- Machine learning for signal processing; VLSI implementation of DSP algorithms
